 Early voting ends today in Georgia after record turnout
 By Marc Teichner FOX 5 Atlanta 2026 Elections Published  October 30, 2026 5:57 AM EDT Share
 Copy Link 
 Email 
 Facebook 
 Twitter 
 LinkedIn 
 Reddit 
 Published  October 30, 2026 5:57 AM EDT Final day for early voting in Georgia 
 More than 2.5 million Georgians had cast early ballots, setting a midterm record with one day of voting left. Friday is the final day of early voting before Election Day on Tuesday. FOX 5 Atlanta's Marc Teichner reporting. 
 The Brief
 More than 2.5 million Georgians had cast early ballots, setting a midterm record with one day of voting left. 
 About 2.4 million voted in person, surpassing the previous midterm record of 2.2 million set in 2022. 
 Friday is the final day of early voting before Election Day on Tuesday. 
 ATLANTA - Georgia’s early voting turnout had topped 2.5 million ballots with one day remaining, setting a record for a midterm election, according to figures cited in a Friday report from DeKalb County. 
 Voters who do not cast a ballot Friday will have to wait until Election Day on Tuesday.
 What we know:
 About 2.4 million of the early ballots were cast in person, far exceeding the previous midterm record of 2.2 million set in 2022. 
 RELATED: Georgia voting history: From exclusion to battleground state 
 Mail-in absentee voting was down by about half, according to the Secretary of State's office, but the overall number of early ballots was still higher than in the previous midterm cycle.
 RELATED: What Georgia’s elected offices do, from Senate to agriculture 
 Secretary of State Brad Raffensperger said earlier in the week that turnout was running about 5% to 7% higher than in 2022, despite having one fewer day of early voting.
 Check voting hours and locations
 Voters planning to cast a ballot Friday were urged to check their early voting location and hours in advance, since they may differ from their assigned Election Day polling place. Click here to check voter registration status and find early voting locations.

 Information for the above comes from the Secretary of State's website and MVP page (links above).
